reason: The checker question is 'is the static type of this expression `any`, and is it used where `any` leaks (member access, call, assignment or argument to a non-any declared type, destructuring, spread, JSX tag)?'. Nearly every fixture operand is an identifier declared `any` elsewhere (`declare const x: any`), so the port can only name sources that are `any` by library signature (JSON.parse). An explicit `(x as any)` is ALLOWED by TSLint (line 131), so the syntax of an any-cast cannot serve as a proxy. 0/65 on fixtures. Checker APIs: getTypeAtLocation, getContextualType (:319, parameter type at an argument), getBaseTypes, getSymbolAtLocation + getAliasedSymbol, getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol (:427-461).

evidence.why: `x.foo;` is flagged only because `declare const x: any` (line 40); the same member access on a typed object is fine
`takesNumber(x, x)` is flagged because the parameters are declared number; `takesAny(x, x)` (line 48) has the same syntax and is valid
`(x as any).whatchamacallit;` is explicitly allowed; a syntactic 'as any' heuristic produces an FP here
